in_hebrew.name: מלכוס
in_hebrew.meaning: מלך מלכים הוא המלך המשיח עבדו של אלוהים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם מלכוס נגזר מהמילה העברית 'מלך' שפירושה 'מלך' או 'שולט'. הוא קשור לאמונה היהודית והנוצרית כאחד, והוא מופיע בברית החדשה ככינוי לאחד מעובדי הכהן הגדול שנכח בגנ היסמין כאשר יהודה איש קריות בגד בישוע. השם מלכוס מייצג את המושג של שירות ומסירות לאלוהים.

in_greek.name: Μαλχός
in_greek.meaning: ο υπηρέτης του Θεού, ο βασιλιάς
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μαλχός προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή λέξη 'מלך' που σημαίνει 'βασιλιάς' ή 'άρχοντας'. Στο πλαίσιο της Καινής Διαθήκης, ο Μαλχός αναφέρεται ως ο υπηρέτης του αρχιερέα κατά τη σύλληψη του Ιησού στο Κήπο της Γεθσημανή. Το όνομα συμβολίζει την υπηρεσία και την αφοσίωση προς τον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Malchus
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Malchus is derived from the Hebrew word 'מלך' meaning 'king' or 'ruler'. In Christian tradition, Malchus is known as the servant of the high priest present at Jesus' arrest in the Garden of Gethsemane. The name signifies devotion and service to God, reflecting a spirit of humility and obedience.

in_english.name: Malchus
in_english.meaning: King's servant or devoted to God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Malchus originates from the Hebrew 'מלך' (malak) meaning 'king' and is associated with a servant or devotee of God. In the New Testament, Malchus is the name of the high priest's servant who lost his ear during Jesus' arrest. The name Malchus symbolizes humility, service, and loyalty, reflecting the values of Christian faith and tradition.

pronunciation.biblical: מלכוס (pronounced as Mal-khos in biblical Hebrew)

biblical_reference.note: Malchus was the servant of the high priest Caiaphas who had his ear cut off by Peter during Jesus' arrest.

data.cultural_impact: Malchus was the name of a notable figure in the New Testament who is remembered for his betrayal of Jesus Christ. In the Gospel of John, Malchus is identified as a servant in the temple guard who cuts off the ear of the high priest's servant, Malchus, during the arrest of Jesus. This acted as a prelude to Jesus' trial and eventual crucifixion. The name ‘Malchus’ has since become synonymous with betrayal, treachery, and deceit.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian theology, the name ‘Malchus’ holds a significant spiritual significance as it serves as a reminder of the power of temptation and the consequences of giving in to it. Malchus, the betrayer, represents the force of darkness that can lead even the closest of companions to abandon their faith and allegiance to their savior. This event serves as a warning against putting materialistic and worldly desires above spiritual commitment and loyalty to one’s beliefs. The character of Malchus illustrates the importance of staying steadfast in faith and not allowing fear or temptation to sway us from our moral and ethical values.
